questions.md:
A belt drive is used to transmit power from a DC motor to the headstock of a lathe. The DC motor shaft rotates at a constant speed of 1200 rpm. The centre distance between the shafts of the belt drive is 1.85 m. The speed reduction ratio is 3.5, and the angle of contact on the smaller pulley is 4.15 radians. The larger pulley has a diameter of 80 cm. The initial belt tension is 850 N and the coefficient of friction is 0.25. Sketch the arrangement and calculate the following:

i) Power transmitted by the belt drive.
ii) Length of the belt.
iii) Width of the belt, if the permissible tension is 8 kN per metre width of the belt.

A belt drive transmits power between two pulleys which are 2 m apart, with a speed reduction ratio of 4 and an angle of contact of 3.81 radians. The diameter of the larger pulley is 100 cm and the driver pulley runs at 400 rpm. The initial tension in the belt is 0.95 kN and the coefficient of friction is 0.28. Calculate the length of the belt, the power transmitted and the width of the belt if the permissible tension per metre width of the belt is 10 kN.

Power is transmitted between two shafts 4 m apart using two pulleys, both rotating counterclockwise, with a velocity ratio of unity. The length of the belt is 11.142 m and the coefficient of friction is 0.3. Determine the size of the two pulleys and the tensions on both sides of the belt if the initial tension is 0.75 kN.

questions.skill: Designing compound train for maximum ratio
questions.md:
The following gear wheels are available to form a compound gear train. Sketch the arrangement of the gear train using four shafts to obtain the highest velocity ratio at the output shaft, and calculate the same. Also mention the conditions used to achieve it.

| Gear | Type | No. of teeth | Module (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Spur | 92 | 2 |
| B | Spur | 40 | 3 |
| C | Spur | 30 | 2 |
| D | Spur | 75 | 2 |
| E | Spur | 60 | 3 |
| F | Spur | 45 | 3 |
| G | Helical | 95 | 3 |
| H | Helical | 120 | 3 |
| I | Helical | 35 | 2 |
| J | Helical | 70 | 2 |
| K | Helical | 80 | 2 |
| L | Helical | 30 | 3 |
| M | Helical | 57 | 2 |

A compound gear train consists of six gear wheels A, B, C, D, E and F. A is the driver gear and F is the driven gear, having 100 and 16 teeth respectively. Gear A meshes with gear B having 60 teeth, and gears B and C are integral and concentric. Gear C has 80 teeth and meshes with gear D having 100 teeth. Gears D and E are mounted on the same shaft, and gear E, having 50 teeth, meshes with gear F. Sketch the arrangement of the gears and determine the velocity ratio.

A simple gear train, as shown in the figure, has four gears A, B, C and D. Gear A is the driver and gear D is the driven gear; gears B and C are intermediate gears. The driving gear A rotates anticlockwise at 300 rpm. The numbers of teeth on gears A, B, C and D are 30, 90, 60 and 120 respectively. Determine:

(i) the speed of the driven gear,
(ii) the speeds of rotation of the intermediate gears,
(iii) the velocity ratio of the gear train.

*See the figure in the paper.*

A chemical company planning to install a coal-fired boiler in its plant for process heating is weighing different technical options due to investment constraints. The steam generation capacity required is 5000 kg per hour at a pressure of 0.56 MPa and a temperature of $220^\circ$C. The feed water is available from a nearby reservoir at an average temperature of $30^\circ$C. The coal consumption is 1500 kg/h, with a calorific value of 24 MJ/kg. Assess the improvement in boiler efficiency if the following accessories are used:

i) An economizer, which will increase the feed water temperature by $58^\circ$C and reduce coal consumption by 14%.
ii) An air preheater, which will reduce coal consumption by 20%.
iii) Both economizer and air preheater, whose combined effect will reduce coal consumption by 30%.

A gas-fired boiler produces superheated steam at 100 bar from feedwater at $45^\circ$C, with a steam flow rate of 12 kg/s. Fuel gas is burned at a rate of 1.5 tonnes per hour, with a GCV of 46 MJ/kg, and the boiler efficiency is 88%. Find the condition of the steam produced.

A steam boiler produces 6000 kg of steam per hour at a pressure of 0.56 MPa and a temperature of $230^\circ$C. The feed water temperature is $25^\circ$C. The fuel consumption is 20 kg/min, with a calorific value of 24 MJ/kg. Assess the improvement in boiler efficiency if the following accessories are used:

i) An economizer, which will increase the feed water temperature to $63^\circ$C and reduce coal consumption by 10%.
ii) An air preheater, which will reduce coal consumption by 22%.

The following observations were recorded during a test on a 4-stroke engine: bore = 15 cm, stroke = 20 cm, camshaft speed = 250 rpm, mean effective pressure = 8 bar, fuel consumption = 0.0013 kg/s, calorific value of the fuel = 43900 kJ/kg. Determine the indicated thermal efficiency.

The following data refer to a twin-cylinder IC engine generating power in every revolution of the crankshaft: total stroke volume = 1.5 litres, number of cycles per revolution = 1800 (as printed; likely cycles per minute), mean effective pressure = 0.32 MPa, fuel consumption = 0.00675 m³/h, density of fuel = 800 kg/m³, calorific value of the fuel = 45000 kJ/kg. Determine the indicated thermal efficiency.

The following observations were recorded during a test on an IC engine: net load on the brake drum = 36 kg, camshaft speed = 250 rpm, fuel consumption = 0.003 kg/s, diameter of the brake drum = 2 m, calorific value of the fuel = 43900 kJ/kg. Determine the brake thermal efficiency and the brake specific fuel consumption.

questions.skill: Heat added in boiler and superheater
questions.md:
250 kg of feed water enters the boiler at a temperature of $27^\circ$C. Steam at a pressure of $1.5\ \text{N/mm}^2$ leaves the boiler 17.5% wet and enters the superheater, where it is superheated to a temperature of $310^\circ$C. Further, from the superheater the steam is led to a heat exchanger for process heating, where it loses 65.8% of its enthalpy. Determine the following:

i) Total heat supplied to water in the boiler.
ii) Total heat supplied to steam in the superheater.
iii) The condition and related parameter of the steam at the exit point of the heat exchanger.

Assume the specific heat of water as $4.187$ kJ/kgK and that of superheated steam as $2.25$ kJ/kgK.

questions.skill: Heat added in boiler and superheater
questions.md:
500 kg of wet steam at a pressure of 0.6 MPa is generated in a boiler per hour. The temperature of the feed water is $20^\circ$C and the total heat added in the boiler is 1236 MJ/h. The steam from the boiler enters the superheater after a heat loss of 300 kJ/kg, where its temperature is to be raised to $200^\circ$C. Determine:

(i) The dryness fraction of the steam at the entry point of the superheater.
(ii) The heat absorbed per hour in the superheater.

questions.skill: Heat added in boiler and superheater
questions.md:
A boiler produces 1200 kg of steam per hour at a pressure of 12 bar and a dryness fraction of 0.85. This steam is then passed through a superheater, where its degree of superheat becomes $150^\circ$C above the saturation temperature. The feedwater supplied to the boiler is at a temperature of $40^\circ$C. Determine:

a) The total heat added per hour in the boiler to convert the feedwater into wet steam.
b) The total heat absorbed per hour in the superheater to raise the temperature of the steam.

(Assume $C_p = 4.18$ kJ/kgK and $C_{sup} = 2.25$ kJ/kgK.)
